A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PMA/CC1M study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material support reliable comparison. The additional reviewer-response page in v3 is included in this assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original adversarial-attack evaluations on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k, and CC1M, including ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds CLIP evaluation, visual examples, and empirical loss analyses in its supplement and appended response.

M1.justification: The PM loss, two-stage PMA updates, Algorithm 1, and ensemble procedures are retained. The CLIP experiment does not document a new PMA component or altered attack procedure.

E1.justification: Section 14 adds a focused image–text matching evaluation using CLIP on CC1M with paired captions and within-batch negatives. v1 uses CC1M for image-prediction consistency evaluation. The original datasets and classification tasks remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 of the appended response adds targeted-cross-entropy PGD, PGDcet, against PGDce and PGDpm on four model/dataset cases. v1 discusses targeted CE mathematically but does not evaluate this comparator in its PGD loss comparison. Existing comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: The added CLIP experiment uses perturbation budgets of 1/255, 2/255, and 3/255, batch size 32, and within-batch negatives. New diagnostic evaluations report PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and CE-loss measurements. Previously stated benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a one-image attack case study, a PGDpm probability-margin trajectory, and targeted-versus-untargeted CE and average-loss diagnostics. These supplement the retained stage-length, restart, optimizer, and loss-weight ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-controlled repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new average CE-loss values are point estimates; the existing attack-restart analyses are unchanged.

E6.justification: Results in the original Tables 2–14 and Figure 1 are retained. Added Table 15 reports CLIP robustness under PMA of 21.16%, 9.40%, and 5.45% at the three respective budgets. Figure 2 and response Tables 1–3 add visual-example, trajectory, targeted-CE, and loss measurements.

T1.justification: The PM definition, gradient decomposition, attack equations, and relative-robustness definition are unchanged. The response adds empirical illustrations and explanations, without a new formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about PMA's attack strength, efficient ensembles, CC1M construction, and the robustness gap between the evaluated datasets. The additional experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: The response adds interpretations of targeted CE's contrasting behavior on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, explains why CE loss alone cannot rank attacks, and expands the rationale for CC1M and relative robustness. Section 14 explicitly acknowledges the CC1M–ImageNet domain mismatch.

D1.justification: v3 supplies batch and negative-sampling details for CLIP, clarifies that Table 6 uses the full ImageNet test set, and identifies Fudan's CFFF computing platform. These are additional disclosures; the original RTX 3090 runtime setup is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Huang et al., 'Detecting backdoor samples in contrastive language image pretraining,' as reference 43 in the LID discussion. The existing LDReg reference becomes 44. The broader positioning relative to MD and other attacks is unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains largely verbatim. v3 expands and renumbers supplementary sections, appends a reviewer-response page, adds acknowledgements, and updates the corresponding-author footnote.

P2.justification: v3 adds supplementary Figure 2 and Table 15 plus three diagnostic tables in the response. The response also redisplays the new image example and CLIP table. Existing displays remain substantially unchanged, with appendix reflow and relocation of Table 14.

improvement.justification: The visual example, targeted-CE and loss diagnostics, and CLIP experiment provide useful empirical support absent from v1. The gain is limited: the core findings remain unchanged, CLIP configuration details are sparse, and some additions remain in a separate response page that duplicates supplementary content.
